dīligenter

adverb · Wiktionary

carefully, attentively, thoroughly

The everyday word for doing a thing with care: looking, reading, keeping, looking after. Cūrā tē dīligenter is Cicero’s “take good care of yourself”. From dīligēns, attentive, careful (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • accūrātē — carefully, with pains; exactly

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 2.1.30: accūrātē agātur, doctē et dīligenter (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 16.5 (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Of work done with pains and precision; Lewis & Short gives dīligenter, studiōsē, exquīsītē as its synonyms.

Examples

  • Fac ita ut jussī. — Faciam. — At dīligenter. — Fīet. — At mātūrē. — Fīet.

    Do as I told you. — I will. — Carefully, mind. — It shall be done. — And promptly. — It shall be done.Ter. Eun. 207–208

  • tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam. cūrā tē dīligenter. valē.

    Let me know when to expect you. Take good care of yourself. Goodbye.Cic. Fam. 16.18.3

  • sed dīligenter intuēre hās nēniās: quantam sub titulīs ūtilitātem reperiēs!

    but look closely at these trifles: how much use you will find under their titles!Phaedr. 4.2.3–4

  • accūrātē agātur, doctē et dīligenter

    let it be done with pains, skill and carePlaut. Capt. 2.1.30 (Lewis & Short)

See also carefully, listen carefully, pay attention!, attention, care.
